title: Weakness: no meal logged, so the alert waits for the rise
description: Glucose rises with no logged meal. Risk stays below the 35% alert threshold until the rise has begun: the alert fires at 14:50 (glucose 93 mg/dL, up from 70 at 14:35), 45 min before glucose first exceeds 180 mg/dL (15:35). With a logged meal (first scenario) the warning comes earlier. Stepping in 1-hour jumps skips the alert (14:45: 31%); the risk-history panel still shows it. What-ifs are recorded at 13:45 only.

primary.label: vs a zero-carb meal at the same time (isolates the carb content)

secondary.label: vs no meal (also includes the model's learned meal-timing expectation)

notes: Meals under 30 g are unreliable in this model: few training meals are that small and the audited small-meal differences are unstable.

joint_support.caveat: Training-support check: it flags meal inputs with no comparable example in the training data. It is not evidence that the forecast is wrong, and inputs inside the training range do not make a forecast accurate.

result.disclaimer: Simulated what-if scenario. The hypothetical meal was never added to the patient record. Differences are learned associations of the forecasting models, not causal physiological effects. Not medical advice and not a treatment recommendation.
